seoTitle: How to Fix PayPal Money Pending Status (2026)
metaDescription: PayPal's own help documentation defines exactly what Pending, In Progress, Voided, Expired, and Denied mean for an order, and what to do about each one.
intro: A "Pending" tag on money you're owed is unsettling, but PayPal's own help documentation is more specific about what it means than the label alone suggests. An order is an agreement between buyer and seller, and Pending just means the seller hasn't collected the payment yet, not that anything has gone wrong. This guide walks through PayPal's official explanation of order statuses, what triggers each one, the 30-day window they run on, and where to go if a pending payment needs a nudge.

steps.heading: What "Pending" means
steps.body: PayPal's help article is direct about this: an order authorizes a seller to eventually charge the buyer's account for a purchase, and a Pending status means the seller received the order but hasn't captured the payment yet. Nothing is broken at this stage. The money is reserved, not charged, until the seller acts.

image.caption: PayPal's support article explaining what an order is and why it shows as pending, with the full list of possible statuses below it.

steps.heading: Check the status in your Activity feed
steps.body: The current status of any order appears in your account's Activity section, under "Payment status." Check there before assuming anything is wrong; the label tells you exactly which of PayPal's six defined states the order is currently in.

steps.heading: Know the difference between the statuses
steps.body: PayPal defines six possible order statuses. Pending means the seller hasn't accepted payment yet, sometimes deliberately, waiting until the buyer receives the item. In Progress means the seller accepted only part of the amount. Complete means the full amount was accepted. Voided means the seller cancelled the payment. Expired means the 30-day window ran out with no action. Denied means the buyer's bank or card issuer rejected the charge outright, a status covered in more detail in the last step below.

steps.heading: Understand why sellers wait before completing an order
steps.body: Most sellers complete an order within a few days as a matter of course: for physical goods, typically once they're ready to ship; for services, rentals, or stays, once the purchase has been delivered. That delay is normal and built into how orders work, not a sign that a seller is sitting on a payment without reason.

steps.heading: Remember the 30-day expiration
steps.body: An order can only show as pending for up to 30 days. After that, it either completes, gets voided, or automatically expires. If a payment you're waiting on is approaching that window, reach out before it lapses, not after. An expired order generally needs to be rearranged from scratch.

steps.heading: Contact the seller if it's stuck
steps.body: If an order looks stalled, PayPal's Send and Request money page is where you'd search for that person by name, username, email, or mobile number to reach them or review the transaction. For an expired payment specifically, PayPal's own guidance is to contact the seller directly to rearrange it, since PayPal itself won't reinstate an expired order automatically.

image.caption: The Send and Request money screen, used to search for a contact by name, username, email, or mobile number.

steps.heading: If the status says Denied instead of Pending
steps.body: A Denied status is a different problem from a Pending one: it means the buyer's bank or card issuer refused the charge, and PayPal's documentation is clear that this needs to be resolved with that bank or card issuer, not through PayPal support. The seller will typically need to create a new order once the underlying payment issue is fixed.

troubleshooting.problem: An order has been Pending for close to 30 days
troubleshooting.cause: The seller hasn't captured the payment yet, and the automatic 30-day expiration window is approaching.
troubleshooting.fix: Contact the seller before the window closes. Once an order expires, PayPal won't reinstate it automatically; the seller has to set up the payment again from scratch.

troubleshooting.problem: An order shows Denied even though funds are available
troubleshooting.cause: The decline happens at the buyer's bank or card issuer, for reasons PayPal itself doesn't control or see the details of.
troubleshooting.fix: Contact the bank or card issuer directly to find out why the charge was refused, then have the seller create a new order once it's resolved.

faq.question: What does a "Pending" order status mean?
faq.answer: The seller received the order but hasn't captured the payment yet. The money is reserved on the buyer's account, not charged, until the seller completes it.

faq.question: How long can an order stay pending?
faq.answer: Up to 30 days. After that it either completes, gets voided by the seller, or automatically expires.

faq.question: What's the difference between Voided and Expired?
faq.answer: Voided means the seller actively cancelled the payment. Expired means the 30-day window ran out with no action from anyone.

faq.question: What does "In Progress" mean?
faq.answer: The seller accepted only part of the payment amount. The remainder stays outstanding until they capture the rest or the order otherwise resolves.

faq.question: What should I do if my order shows as Denied?
faq.answer: Contact the bank or card issuer for the decline details. PayPal's documentation states this status means the charge was refused at the bank level, something PayPal itself can't resolve.

faq.question: Can I get an expired order reinstated?
faq.answer: Not automatically. PayPal's guidance is to contact the seller directly to rearrange payment once an order has expired.

verifiedNote: Re-checked against PayPal's official help article on order statuses in September 2026. The original draft's definitions of Pending, In Progress, Complete, Voided, Expired, and Denied, and the 30-day window, all matched PayPal's current documentation verbatim, so no factual corrections were needed. Changes here are structural: the redundant second explanation of Denied was consolidated into one place, and two troubleshooting entries were added for the two situations most worth acting on early, an order nearing its 30-day expiration and a Denied status a buyer wants explained.
